Format RiskMap Results as a Table

Source: R/auxiliary.R, R/cross_validation.R
to_table.Rd

Converts a fitted "RiskMap" model, cross-validation results or polygon predictions into a table that renders directly in Quarto, R Markdown, HTML, LaTeX and the R console.

Usage

to_table(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap'
to_table(object, digits = 3, col_names = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.RiskMap'
to_table(object, digits = 3, col_names = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
to_table(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap_cross_validation'
to_table(object, digits = 3, col_names = NULL, reference = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.RiskMap_cross_validation'
to_table(object, digits = 3, col_names = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fit from glgpm() or its summary(), a cross-validation from assess_prediction() or its summary(), or a prediction over boundaries from predict() (see to_table.RiskMap_prediction()).

...

Additional arguments passed to knitr::kable().

digits

A non-negative integer giving the number of decimal places used to display numeric results. Small values get more (see Details).

col_names

Optional column names, replacing the default headers.

reference

For a cross-validation, optional name of the model that the others are compared with, as in its summary().

Value

An object of class "knitr_kable" that can be rendered directly.

Details

This function creates a presentation-ready summary table from a fitted "RiskMap" model or cross-validation results for multiple models. Use coef() or summary() when numeric results are required for further analysis.

Numeric values have digits decimal places. Values that are compared, the estimate and confidence limits of a parameter or one metric across models, share one notation and one number of decimal places. When one of them is smaller in size than 10^(-digits), they get as many decimal places as the smallest needs for two significant digits. They are in scientific notation when that takes more than six decimal places, or when one of them is a million or more in size. Zeros and missing values don't count.

The table of a fit or its summary has

  • the regression coefficients with their estimates and confidence intervals,

  • the parameters of the spatial process,

  • the variances of the random effects,

  • the parameters of the family that were estimated, such as the measurement error variance of a Gaussian model.

The table of a cross-validation or its summary has a row for each model, with its scores, their differences from a reference model with their standard errors in brackets, and its PIT_area with the limit of a correct model.

See also

glgpm(), summary.RiskMap_cross_validation()

Examples

data(italy_sim)

fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp(),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)
to_table(fit)
#> 
#> 
#> |                         | Estimate| Lower limit| Upper limit|
#> |:------------------------|--------:|-----------:|-----------:|
#> |(Intercept)              |    9.323|       7.701|      10.946|
#> |Spatial process var.     |    4.849|       1.820|      12.924|
#> |Spatial corr. scale (km) |   39.015|       2.777|     548.084|
#> |Measurement error var.   |    0.179|       0.133|       0.239|
to_table(fit, digits = 1)
#> 
#> 
#> |                         | Estimate| Lower limit| Upper limit|
#> |:------------------------|--------:|-----------:|-----------:|
#> |(Intercept)              |      9.3|         7.7|        10.9|
#> |Spatial process var.     |      4.8|         1.8|        12.9|
#> |Spatial corr. scale (km) |     39.0|         2.8|       548.1|
#> |Measurement error var.   |      0.2|         0.1|         0.2|
